environment.reused_deliverable: ocor_runtime.c8_agent.AgentKernel (the existing, predating-this-session single-agent kernel -- sandboxed execution, token budgets, identify-or-abstain -- already reused unmodified by OCOR-DEV-0031's mission thread) is left completely untouched; this task's own ocor_runtime.c8.orchestrator is a new, separate module built around it. ocor_runtime.c6_capabilities.CapabilityAuthority and ocor_runtime.c3_store.AtomicOutboxStore (both sealed, reused across many prior tasks this session) are composed exclusively through their own public issue()/authorize()/write()/get() methods, never modified.

commands.command: design: AgentRunOrchestrator.assign()/commit()/handoff()/register_dissent() each require a real capability lease authorized via the sealed CapabilityAuthority.authorize() before doing anything else, and write their resulting record through the sealed AtomicOutboxStore.write() using the store's own authoritative_writer as writer_id -- the orchestrator is the sole caller of write(), never an agent. This structurally realizes the task's three negative claims rather than merely testing for them: (1) an agent cannot self-grant a capability, since authorize() only accepts a lease the authority itself already issued and an agent has no reference to the authority; (2) an agent cannot mutate canonical state directly, since the sealed store's own single-writer boundary (SingleWriterViolation) refuses any writer_id other than the orchestrator's; (3) dissent can never be suppressed, since Dissent is a frozen dataclass and the class exposes no removal/retraction/update method -- dissents is a read-only, append-only tuple.

genuine design bug found and fixed before sealing: the test's own second-commit step (by a new agent, after a real handoff) raised a real ocor_runtime.errors.ConcurrencyConflict from the sealed AtomicOutboxStore -- commit()'s original idempotency_key was a fixed f'commit:{task_id}' with no attempt counter, so a genuinely different second commit (different agent_id) reused the identical idempotency key as the first, correctly refused by the sealed store as an idempotency-key reuse for a different write request. Fixed by deriving a real per-aggregate attempt counter from the store's own current document version (store.get(aggregate_id)) for both assign() and commit(), using it in both idempotency_key and expected_version -- a correct, version-aware optimistic-concurrency write.

requirement_results.command: assign, commit and dissent all write real, retrievable canonical documents through the sealed AtomicOutboxStore
a handoff correctly reassigns both the assignment and the commitment to the new agent, and the new agent can recommit using its own real lease
a handoff without a reason is refused
committing an unassigned task, or handing off an uncommitted one, is refused with UNKNOWN_TASK

a fabricated lease id never issued by the authority, a lease for a different capability, a lease scoped to a different resource, and a revoked lease are all refused identically -- no agent action can substitute for a real authority-issued grant
a real, direct store.write() call using an agent's own id as writer_id is refused by the sealed store's single-writer boundary
registered dissents remain append-only with no removal/retraction/update method exposed, and a Dissent record itself is frozen and cannot be mutated in place
a dissent without a reason is refused
full local pytest regression with a real live PostgreSQL DSN set, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: This task builds the smallest contract-compliant slice of task assignment/commitment/handoff/dissent; it does not itself model a full team hierarchy, escalation policy, or dissent-resolution workflow -- a future task could layer those on top of AgentRunOrchestrator's own append-only dissent record and versioned canonical writes without needing to touch this file.

handoff() and register_dissent() intentionally do not derive expected_version from the store for their own new per-index aggregate ids (urn:ocor:agentrun:handoff:{task_id}:{n}, urn:ocor:agentrun:dissent:{task_id}:{n}), since each such aggregate_id is written to exactly once and is never revisited -- correct as designed, but a future extension mutating an existing handoff/dissent record (not currently supported) would need the same version-aware pattern already applied to assign()/commit().

AgentRunOrchestrator does not itself invoke ocor_runtime.c8_agent.AgentKernel -- it governs the team-level lifecycle around an agent's work, not the agent's own model invocation; a future integration task would compose both, the same way OCOR-DEV-0031's mission thread already composes AgentKernel with other retained components.

The pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it produces the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated regression failures documented in every prior evidence file this session.
